item.title: Local call for resolution on secretary and caretakers' school dispute
item.description: A local senator has called on all parties to come together to resolve the school secretary and caretakers' dispute. Robbie Gallagher has called all relevant stakeholders to come together and work towards a constructive resolution to the ongoing dispute. Senator Gallagher acknowledged the vital role of secretaries and caretakers in school communities. item.title: Night Navigation season moves South
item.description: The attention turns back to the Night Navigation season this Saturday night as the Skibbereen & District Car club host their Carbery trial. The event is round 4 of the National championship and will be based from the Bandon Rugby club with crews set to compete over a route of 75 miles. item.title: Local 'concern' over adult asylum seekers placed in children’s care
item.description: 192 adult asylum seekers were placed in children’s accommodation over the past three years. Tulsa had mistakenly placed the international protection applicants in children’s care, before establishing they were over 18. This year there have been 86 such cases, that’s more than double the 2023 figures. Advertisement The information was obtained by Cavan-Monaghan TD Matt Carthy. item.title: Smith: 'Urgent need to enact legacy framework'
item.description: The Taoiseach has said he believes that there is a "sincere commitment" on behalf of the British Government on the implementation of the Legacy Framework. Local TD Brendan Smith asked the Taoiseach about the framework in the Dáil this week. Deputy Smith outlined that there is an urgent need to enact legacy legislation to give effect to the provisions outlined in the framework. item.title: National league fixtures are released
item.description: Monaghan will open their Division 1 league campaign when they welcome Armagh to St Tiernachs Park Clones on Sunday January 25th at 2pm. That will be 1 of 4 home games the Farney side will have as Mayo, Galway and Donegal will all be hosted by Gabriel Bannigans side. item.title: Suspended sentence for Crossmaglen man over waste offences
item.description: A Crossmaglen man has been handed a 18 months suspended sentence over waste offences. Eugene McEntee 53, of Drummuckavall Road, Crossmaglen was sentenced at Newry Crown Court for breaches of waste legislation. He was given 18 months imprisonment, suspended for two years for these waste offences. Advertisement The offences related to the unauthorised keeping of controlled waste at the site on the Alley Road, Crossmaglen, controlled by Mr McEntee. item.title: Plans to extend Ulster Canal set to be lodged
item.description: Waterways Ireland say they intend to apply for permission to extend the Ulster Canal in Clones. In an application submitted to Monaghan County Council for pre-validation they say the purposed development would run the townlands of Clonlura, Clonnagore, Clonoony, Drumsloe and Roranna. The development will consist of the restoration and rebuilding of approximately 3.75km section of the historical Ulster Canal corridor for tourism and recreation. item.title: 'Gift of a Lift' campaign launched in Monaghan
item.description: A festive season gets into full swing, Monaghan County Council is urging everyone to plan their journey home and make road safety a priority. The annual 'Gift of a Lift' campaign was launched today. Supported locally by An Garda Síochána, the National Ambulance Service and Monaghan Fire and Civil Protection, this campaign encourages people to give the ultimate gift this Christmas - a safe lift home. item.title: Mary King
item.description: Mary King Crover, Broomfield, Castleblayney, Co. Monaghan. Mary King died on Thursday, 4th December 2025. In her 89th year. Peacefully, surrounded by her cherished family, in the wonderful care of the management & staff of Killanny House, Castleross Nursing Home, Carrickmacross. Predeceased by her son Francis, her parents; Patrick & Bridget and her brother Tommy. Sadly missed and remembered with love by her beloved family; her brother Paddy and her sister Kathleen Casey, her sister-in-law Rosale
